redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed from 3 (50-69%) to 5 (>89%). Definition: Is the register integrated with the government's national data exchange system?
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed as 'Planned'. Sierra Leone's national data-exchange platform (a Government Service Bus/Data Exchange Layer) is itself only now being built: an NCRA-MoCTI MoU (May 2024) describes a future Data Exchange Layer, and a World Bank-funded GSB/X-Road pilot only had its consultants selected in March 2025. No evidence the electoral register is yet connected to any operational national exchange platform; voter-roll linkage to NCRA is a periodic data extraction, not live interoperability.

The voter register is a fully digital, biometric (fingerprint and facial) national database, extracted from NCRA civil-registry data, deployed at 3,300 registration centres nationwide and used to enrol 3,374,258 voters for the June 2023 general election (Carter Center report; Laxton case study) — this supports 'Fully deployed nationwide' rather than 'Partial'.

Definition: Does the government maintain a separate cadastral register?
Comments: Plans for LIMS/cadastre digitization (World Bank), but no operational online system.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed from 2 (Planned) to 3 (Under development). The Sierra Leone Land Administration Project (2022-2028) has moved beyond planning: 13 Continuously Operating Reference Stations were installed in 2025 covering 62,000 km2, a firm has been recruited to develop the Land Information/cadastral system, and land-records digitisation is underway (World Bank ISR, April 2024; UN Global Geospatial presentation). No operational public digital cadastre exists yet, so 'Fully/Partially deployed' is not supported, but active development is.
